clue.text: Kitty takes fish to cauldron

parts.note: a jack is a young pike, a fish
a cauldron is a large cooking pot

explanation.surface: A cat snatches a fish and drops it into a witch's pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money staked or collected, just as a big accumulated prize is.

clue.text: Jolly ordinary chap circumnavigating island

indicators.note: circumnavigating means going all the way around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an ordinary Joe is an average man
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A cheerful everyday fellow sails right round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and humorous, a synonym of jolly.

clue.text: Something reddish-brown, very red poison

parts.note: Cu is the symbol for copper, a reddish-brown metal
rare steak is very red inside

explanation.surface: A reddish-brown substance turns out to be a very red poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract used on arrow tips, a paralysing poison.

clue.text: Unpleasant person, unknown, hiding in birch tree

parts.note: prick is slang for an unpleasant man

indicators.note: hiding in means the unknown letter is tucked inside the next piece

parts.note: to birch is to flog, to lash
in algebra y is an unknown

explanation.surface: A nasty man and a stranger are concealed in a birch tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly ash is a spiny North American shrub or small tree.

clue.text: Ins and outs, as advertised itinerary's held up

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The comings and goings of a trip, as the published schedule is delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'held up' reads the run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea comes in and goes out twice a day, so the flows of water are ins and outs.

clue.text: Maoist leader's penetration of moderate after revolution is a process of assimilation

indicators.note: the Maoist leader's letter penetrates, so it goes inside the other piece
after revolution means the word for moderate is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: so-so means moderate, middling

indicators.note: a leader is the front, so the first letter of Maoist

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Maoist figure infiltrates a moderate movement after a revolution, absorbing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' gives OSOS (the reverse of so-so), and 'penetration of' puts the Maoist leader's M inside it; the surface's politics hides a biology term.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the gradual absorption of fluid through a membrane, hence figuratively soaking up ideas.

clue.text: In need of guidance certainly, having secured very poor grade

indicators.note: having secured means the phrase for certainly holds the grade inside it

parts.note: of course means certainly
F is the failing grade in exams

explanation.surface: A student needing direction, sure enough, after scoring a fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has strayed from the planned route needs steering back, so needs guidance.

clue.text: Find flesh by the ear

indicators.note: by the ear means judged as heard rather than as written

parts.note: meat is animal flesh

explanation.surface: Locate the flesh beside the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across or encounter someone is to find them.

clue.text: Dolly so red-faced?

definitions.meaning: Dolly the cloned sheep would be like a sheep

explanation.walkthrough: Dolly was the sheep cloned in Scotland in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling foolish and embarrassed, as a blushing person is, describes this word.

clue.text: Reserve team inferior to East Ham

indicators.note: inferior to means placed below, as the team follows in this down light
to ham is to overact wildly, so the word is played about with

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: Keep back a team weaker than East Ham, an east London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' rearranges EAST to SETA; East Ham is a part of London, which disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside money is to reserve or keep it for later.

clue.text: Council for a fitter dog

definitions.meaning: the Council for Registered Gas Installers, the former UK body with which gas fitters had to register, went by these initials
a short-legged Welsh breed favoured by the Queen

explanation.walkthrough: CORGI was the UK registration scheme for gas fitters until 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a dog breed, and the acronym was the British gas-fitters' registration council.

clue.text: Motto of the un-14 16 team? Whatever rocks your boat!

definitions.meaning: a team that is not synchronised (14) in swimming (16) would each use their own stroke, a playful motto
an idiom meaning each to their own taste

explanation.walkthrough: 14 and 16 are SYNCHRONISED SWIMMING, so the un-synchronised team swims in assorted styles.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says people have their own preferred ways, the same idea as whatever pleases you.

clue.text: See 10
Composition requiring oxygen and bodily fluid?

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
pus is the fluid from an infected wound

explanation.surface: A piece of music that apparently needs air and something nasty from the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word for a work, used for a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Girl clutching to individual, Marie

indicators.note: clutching means holding the other pieces within

parts.note: Annette is a girl's name
taken as written
I is one, an individual

explanation.surface: A girl hugs one person called Marie.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie is the first name of the French queen, so her surname completes it.

clue.text: Drenching my own missis, ridiculous sport

indicators.note: something ridiculous is all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone soaks their wife and calls it a silly sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges the twenty letters of DRENCHING MY OWN MISSIS; 'missis' is a British slang word for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Olympic discipline of coordinated pool routines, a kind of sport.

clue.text: This, as fierce battle's ending, perhaps?

definitions.text: This, as fierce battle's ending, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters are offered in one possible arrangement among others
a word's ending is its final letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether a truce is what ends a fierce battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AS, FIERCE and E. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce halting the fighting is a natural way for a fierce battle to end.

clue.text: See 14
Seasonal fare in the East London Observer?

definitions.meaning: a Christmas pastry filled with dried fruit
in Cockney rhyming slang ... means eyes, so one is an observer

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, from East London, uses 'mince pies' for eyes; the clue looks like a newspaper title.
explanation.definitionFit: This small fruit pastry is eaten at Christmas, and in Cockney slang it stands for an eye.

clue.text: Beds draw cat needing a snooze, beginning to drop off

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, often just called the cat

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
the beginning of the word drop is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a cat that needs a nap and starts to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges A, SNOOZE and D into SNADEZOO. Beds is Bedfordshire, an English county, where this wildlife park is a big attraction ('draw').
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist draw is an attraction, and this zoo is a famous one in Bedfordshire.

clue.text: Earth, say, provides energy to feed bush, perhaps

indicators.note: to feed means to go into, so the energy letter enters the other word

parts.note: a bush is an example of a plant
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Earth gives the power that nourishes a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a world orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Couple with a jacket on, I gathered

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket

indicators.note: gathered means the word on takes the letter into itself

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pairs up wearing a jacket, or so I understood.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin is to join or attach, as to couple two things.

clue.text: Laugh at dummy

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, imitation or sham, as in a practice exam

explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule someone, and a sham or imitation thing is a dummy one.

clue.text: Latest milk tooth, perhaps, was in front

parts.note: a child's milk tooth could be called a new fang, a tooth that has just come in
led means was in front, leading

explanation.surface: A child's newest baby tooth was the first to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfangled describes something novel and up to date, latest in fashion, often disapprovingly.

clue.text: See 10
A song turning up — here?

indicators.note: in a down light turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Asks whether a song pops up at this point.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in opera, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: This setter's limited, to be fair

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says I am, shortened to I'm
partial means limited, incomplete

explanation.surface: The setter admits his scope is restricted, in fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being even-handed and unbiased is what fair means in judging.

clue.text: Dramatic steps taken to get Brown to step down?

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
go means leave a post, to step down

explanation.surface: Theatrical moves made to force someone named Brown to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests Gordon Brown, the UK prime minister, under pressure to resign when the clue appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a dramatic Argentine dance made of stylised steps.

clue.text: Bomb, say, catching European king from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the whole assembled string is read backwards
catching means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: e.g. is short for for example, so say
a Dane is a European from Denmark
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A bomb, for instance, snaring a European monarch from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts DANER inside EG to make EDANERG, and 'from behind' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown explosive device is a kind of bomb.

clue.text: Enormous bottom on cute figure? Sugar!

indicators.note: in a down light 'on' would stack, but here it means the letter sits before the rest
the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: wee means little and endearing, cute
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A fat behind on an attractive body? Oh, sugar!
explanation.definitionFit: To sugar something is to add sweetness to it, so the imperative is the same verb.
